answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to hold exclusive non-poolable collateral and recompute a sequential memory-hard willow proof every epoch. A fresh zephyr of randomness from the public beacon seeds the computation so prior work cannot be reused or shared across clones. The resulting unique lantern attestation is checked by a quorum that rejects double-committed stake. Attacker cost therefore rises linearly with the number of fake identities because each clone must keep its own live working set and sequential compute, while an honest agent pays the cost only once.
